messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: RStan compilation optimization?
parts:
Following on from the message from Andrew and the help request
from a user, I'd like to try to automate as much as possible:

* removing -g option from compilation

* making sure parser and code generator compile with -O0

* making sure lib compiles with -O3

* making sure we don't have bogus architecture flags (e.g., -core2 for
non core2 machines)

* making sure models are compiled with -O3

I'm afraid if we don't, Stan installations are going to be slow and
thus hurt the user experience and tarnish our reputation.

I found the R.home() function [oddly called Rhome in the doc], but
on my machine it returns:

> R.home()
[1] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources"

rather than "~/.R/. Digging deeper, I saw this on the FAQ:

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html

Starting with R 2.1.0, users can provide personal Makevars configuration
files in $HOME/.R to override the default flags.

Is it an OK practice to just change all the Makevars files without changing
them back? If so, can we just automatically do that from the get go
by doing what Andrew suggests and just writing the files out.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStan compilation optimization?
parts:
On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 4:20:22 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Following on from the message from Andrew and the help request
from a user, I'd like to try to automate as much as possible:

   * removing -g option from compilation

   * making sure parser and code generator compile with -O0

   * making sure lib compiles with -O3

   * making sure we don't have bogus architecture flags (e.g., -core2 for
     non core2 machines)

   * making sure models are compiled with -O3

I'm afraid if we don't, Stan installations are going to be slow and
thus hurt the user experience and tarnish our reputation.

Mostly reasons why we need binary installs. But in the meantime, I think we just need to have the installation directions say to do

Sys.setenv(R_MAKEVARS_USER = "foobar")
options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/"))
install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
Sys.unsetenv("R_MAKEVARS_USER")

so that it will read the non-existent configuration file foobar instead of whatever the hell the user has when installing. Then,

library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast") # or set_cppo("debug")

should achieve the appropriate behavior for Stan models.

It is already frowned upon for an R package to be messing with the Makevars file. We are probably breaking a few packages that work at -O2 but not at -O3. But just take a bodyguard with you to conferences and we should be all right.

Ben
